subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is a typical feature of proprietary software?
options: Anyone may legally redistribute modified copies
It is always free of charge
The source code is closed and usually requires a licence to use
Its source code is freely available to edit
questions.explain: Proprietary software keeps its source code closed and is usually licensed (often paid).

questions.q: Which is an example of how the digital divide can disadvantage some people?
options: All schools receiving identical fast broadband
Students without home internet finding it harder to complete online homework
Everyone owning the latest smartphone
Computers becoming cheaper for everyone equally
questions.explain: The digital divide disadvantages those without access, for example students without home internet struggling with online work.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the Data Protection Act / GDPR?
options: To stop companies using the internet
To make all software free to use
To protect how personal data is collected, stored and used
To prevent any data being stored online
questions.explain: Data protection law governs how personal data is collected, stored and used fairly and securely.

questions.q: One environmental benefit of cloud and remote working can be:
options: Reduced travel and potentially lower energy use per user
Faster broadband for everyone automatically
Increased commuting and travel
Guaranteed elimination of all e-waste
questions.explain: Remote working can cut commuting and may reduce energy use, benefiting the environment.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a cultural impact of widespread technology use?
options: Hard drives spinning faster
Changes to how people communicate, share opinions and access information globally
Increasing the clock speed of processors
Reducing the size of a MAC address
questions.explain: A cultural impact concerns how technology changes society, such as the way people communicate and access information.

questions.q: What is meant by the 'digital divide'?
options: The boundary between two networks
The gap between those who have access to technology and those who do not
The difference between LANs and WANs
The split between hardware and software
questions.explain: The digital divide is the gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not.

questions.q: Which action would breach the Computer Misuse Act?
options: Reading a public web page
Backing up your own files
Buying a licensed copy of software
Accessing someone else's account without permission to steal data
questions.explain: Accessing another person's account without permission to steal data breaches the Computer Misuse Act.

questions.q: A company keeps customers' personal details on an unsecured server with no password. Which law are they most likely breaking?
options: The Computer Misuse Act
Patent law
The Data Protection Act
The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act
questions.explain: Failing to keep personal data secure breaches the Data Protection Act, which requires data to be stored securely.

questions.q: Streaming a copyrighted film from an unofficial site without permission most directly breaks which law?
options: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act
The Data Protection Act
Health and safety law
The Computer Misuse Act
questions.explain: Accessing copyrighted material without permission breaches the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act.

questions.q: What is the main reason for legislation such as the Computer Misuse Act?
options: To force companies to recycle e-waste
To ensure all software is open source
To guarantee everyone has internet access
To make hacking and unauthorised access to systems a criminal offence
questions.explain: The Computer Misuse Act exists to criminalise hacking and unauthorised access to computer systems.

questions.q: Under data protection principles, personal data should be:
options: Collected without telling the person
Kept for as long as possible regardless of need
Accurate, kept secure and used only for stated purposes
Shared freely with anyone who asks
questions.explain: Data protection requires personal data to be accurate, secure and used only for the stated purpose.

questions.q: Why is e-waste an environmental concern?
options: Discarded electronics can contain toxic materials and fill landfill
It only affects software performance
It makes computers run faster
It uses too much network bandwidth
questions.explain: E-waste from discarded electronics can contain toxic materials and add to landfill, harming the environment.

questions.q: Under data protection law (GDPR), what right does an individual have over their personal data?
options: No rights once data is collected
The right to request access to and correction of data held about them
The right to delete any company's entire database
The right to be paid for every website visit
questions.explain: Individuals have rights including accessing and requesting correction of personal data held about them.

questions.q: Why might a business carefully consider the ethical impact before using AI to monitor employees?
options: Because AI cannot store any data
Because it removes the need for any data protection
Because monitoring always increases network speed
Because it could invade privacy and affect employees' trust and wellbeing
questions.explain: Monitoring employees raises ethical concerns about privacy and trust, which a responsible business should weigh up.

questions.q: What is a key feature of open source software?
options: The source code is always kept secret
The source code is available and can be modified by users
It can never be used for free
It cannot be shared with others
questions.explain: Open source software makes its source code available for users to view and modify.

questions.q: Which law makes unauthorised access to computer material illegal?
options: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act
The Computer Misuse Act
The Data Protection Act
The Equality Act
questions.explain: The Computer Misuse Act makes unauthorised access to computer systems (e.g. hacking) illegal.

questions.q: A privacy concern of using social media is that:
options: It cannot store any user data
It removes the need for passwords
Personal information may be collected and shared without full consent
It always slows your internet connection
questions.explain: Social media can collect and share personal information, raising privacy concerns.

questions.q: Copying and distributing software without permission most directly breaks which law?
options: The Data Protection Act
Health and Safety regulations
The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act
The Computer Misuse Act
questions.explain: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act protects creators' work from being copied without permission.

questions.q: Which is an example of technology affecting employment?
options: Computers having no effect on any jobs
Automation replacing some manual jobs while creating new technical roles
Only increasing the number of farming jobs
Stopping all online communication
questions.explain: Automation can replace some jobs while creating new technical ones, changing the workforce.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of open source software compared with proprietary software?
options: Users can study and adapt the source code to their own needs
Its source code is always hidden
It always has guaranteed professional support
It can never contain bugs
questions.explain: Because the source code is available, open source software can be studied and adapted by users.

questions.q: Which action helps reduce the environmental impact of computing?
options: Throwing old devices straight into landfill
Recycling and reusing old equipment and using energy-efficient hardware
Leaving all devices running at full power continuously
Replacing working devices every month
questions.explain: Recycling, reusing equipment and choosing energy-efficient hardware all reduce the environmental impact of computing.

questions.q: Which is a recognised drawback of proprietary software for the user?
options: It never receives any updates
It is impossible to install
Users cannot legally modify the source code and often must pay licence fees
It must always be shared freely
questions.explain: Proprietary software keeps source code closed, so users cannot modify it and usually must pay for a licence.
